title: Already Feeling Behind in September? Your IB Reset
summary: Already feeling behind in September? Use this practical IB DP1 reset to close gaps, plan each week, catch up calmly, and build momentum by November.
body_markdown:
September has a peculiar way of making small problems feel permanent. One confusing Chemistry lesson becomes evidence that you chose the wrong HL. An unfinished reading seems to prove that everyone else is more organized.


If you are already feeling behind in September, the answer is not to study everything at once. Identify what is overdue, what you do not understand, and what merely feels unfamiliar. Then build a weekly system that protects current lessons while repairing earlier gaps.


You do not need to catch up with the entire IB Diploma Programme this week. You need to regain control of the next seven days.


### Your September reset checklist


Start with these actions:


- Put every test, assignment, CAS commitment, and school deadline into one calendar.
- List unfinished work by subject, topic, and required output.
- Separate urgent tasks from important but non-urgent gaps.
- Ask teachers which missing tasks still matter.
- Protect 3-5 focused catch-up blocks each week.
- Review your plan every Friday or Sunday.


This is not a heroic recovery plan. It is a controlled reset designed to carry you into November without sacrificing sleep or allowing new work to accumulate.


Comic showing that panic can make a small September workload cast a much larger shadow


### Decide whether you are behind or simply adjusting


The IB DP combines six subjects with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, and Creativity, Activity, Service. That structure can create the sensation of falling behind before much assessable work has accumulated.


Do not measure progress by how confident your classmates sound. Use evidence instead. Create a one-page audit:


Category Question to ask


Deadlines What must be submitted within the next 14 days?


Understanding Which taught concepts can I not explain without notes?


Practice Which skills have I not applied independently?


Organization Which dates, files, or instructions am I missing?


“I am behind in Biology” is difficult to solve. “I cannot explain membrane transport, and there is a quiz next Thursday” gives you a topic, deadline, and next action.


The[RevisionDojo guide for IB DP1 students](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-for-ib-dp1-students) can help you map each subject by current topic, assessment, level, and weakness.


### Stop treating every task as equally urgent


When everything appears important, students often choose the easiest task. It creates movement without meaningful progress.


Sort your work into three groups:


- **Recover now:** overdue submissions, imminent tests, and prerequisite concepts needed for current lessons.
- **Schedule next:** important gaps that are not blocking this week’s work.
- **Release or clarify:** excessive note rewriting and tasks a teacher confirms no longer require completion.


Talk to teachers before spending an evening repairing an old worksheet. Ask which part of the topic is essential for the next unit. This is not escaping work. It is placing limited time where it has the greatest academic value.


Prioritize consequences as well as deadlines. A weak algebra foundation may affect several future Mathematics topics, so it deserves repeated attention even when smaller tasks are easier to cross off.


### Build a two-track IB DP1 fall term plan


Catching up fails when it replaces current learning. You repair September, then discover that October has moved on without you. Use two tracks instead.


### Protect current lessons


Complete the preparation, practice, and assignments connected to what your class is studying now. After each lesson, close your notes and spend 10-15 minutes retrieving the main ideas from memory. Flag confusion while the lesson is recent.


### Repair one earlier gap at a time


Choose one high-priority weakness and give it 2-3 focused blocks during the week. Do not rotate among six subjects in one evening. Complete a meaningful unit, then move to the next gap.


Day Main purpose


Monday Current HL work and short recall


Tuesday Highest-priority catch-up block


Wednesday Current assignments and one core task


Thursday Targeted questions and second catch-up block


Friday Light review and plan adjustment


Weekend One deeper repair block, buffer time, and rest


Adapt this pattern around your timetable. The[balanced IB study schedule](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-create-a-balanced-ib-study-schedule) and[IB Study Planner](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/study-planner) can turn broad intentions into subject-specific tasks.


### Use methods that reveal gaps quickly


Feeling behind often leads to passive work. Rereading feels reassuring, but familiarity is not the same as being able to retrieve or apply knowledge.


Use a short learning loop:


1. Read the relevant Study Notes for one concept.
2. Close them and explain the idea from memory.
3. Use Flashcards for essential facts, formulas, or terminology.
4. Complete a targeted Questionbank set.
5. Record why each mistake happened.
6. Revisit the weakness after a short delay.


RevisionDojo brings this process together. Its[IB subject note collections](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-subject-note-collections-comprehensive-study-materials) help rebuild understanding without rewriting a textbook. The[IB Questionbank workflow](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-question-bank-or-how-to-use-it-effectively) turns that understanding into usable skill. AI Chat can clarify a misconception, while Grading tools show where written responses may lose marks.


Be precise when asking for help. “Explain cellular respiration” is broad. “Why is oxygen needed at the end of the electron transport chain?” gives AI Chat, a teacher, or a tutor a clear problem to address.


### Keep the IB core visible


TOK, CAS, the Extended Essay, and later coursework can feel like extra subjects. In September, they usually require steady contact rather than constant attention.


Reserve one short weekly core block. You might record a CAS reflection, organize assigned TOK reading, explore an Extended Essay interest, or check coursework instructions. The Coursework Library can clarify the shape of strong work, but always follow your school’s deadlines and academic-integrity guidance.


A short block will not complete a major project. It will keep the next action visible and prevent quiet obligations from becoming urgent ones.


### Know what not to do in September


Do not create a timetable that depends on studying late every night. Do not sacrifice meals, exercise, or sleep to imitate someone else’s routine. Most importantly, do not make beautiful notes for familiar topics while avoiding questions that reveal uncertainty.


You also do not need full Mock Exams or Predicted Papers for material you have barely learned. These tools become more useful once you have enough syllabus coverage to practise timing, integration, and decision-making. In early DP1, short topic sets usually provide clearer feedback.


Do not keep a failing plan because you spent time designing it. The[RevisionDojo time-management guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/time-management-in-ib-9-proven-tools-and-techniques-that-actually-work) recommends concrete blocks and a regular weekly reset. If a 60-minute session repeatedly fails, reduce it to 30 minutes and define a smaller output.


### Use October and November to consolidate


By October, your system should produce evidence. You should know which subjects need more practice, which deadlines surprise you, and which study blocks are sustainable.


During October, continue repairing prerequisite gaps, begin spaced review of September topics, and ask for help when a misunderstanding survives two independent attempts.


During November, review your mistake log, rebalance HL and SL time using actual performance, and use Mock Exams selectively for taught material. Consider Tutors when repeated self-study does not resolve a specific difficulty. Check that CAS and core milestones are recorded too.


A[full IB timetable system](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-stay-organized-with-a-full-ib-timetable) can connect these academic tasks with personal commitments, rest, and buffer time.


### You are not trying to erase September


The first months of the Diploma Programme reveal which systems you need. They are not proof that you should manage everything immediately.


If you are already feeling behind in September, begin with one honest audit, one conversation, and one focused block. Protect current learning while repairing the most consequential gap. Then repeat the process next week.


RevisionDojo is the ultimate IB resource for making that repetition easier. Study Notes, Flashcards, the Questionbank, AI Chat, Grading tools, Predicted Papers, Mock Exams, the Coursework Library, and Tutors each solve a different part of the problem. Together, they turn “I am behind” from a verdict into a workable plan.
